ep02:
Zara looked at her ex's profile before her alarm had finished. Twenty-nine days.

Last night she rang her best friend and said the real reason out loud.

Remy took it well. Remy also made one rule. No looking.

He posted at eleven. A cake tasting.

Zara has opinions about that cake. Professional ones.

At work she is excellent until about ten past nine. By lunch she knows the flavour. Lemon.

It was not research.

At midnight her thumb nearly liked it. So she opens the app instead.

She writes: I keep checking if he's happy.

No advice. It just asks: what are you hoping to find?

She knows the answer. She doesn't type it.

Mute him for twenty-nine days, or one last proper look.

What would you do?

Twenty-eight days.
ep03:
Zara is washing her ex's hoodie at seven in the morning. His wedding is in twenty-eight days. She is going.

Yesterday she muted him. It worked, which left her hands with nothing to do.

The hoodie has lived at the back of her wardrobe since the car park.

Her best friend asked who for.

To give it back. That is the official position.

She sat on the floor and watched the whole cycle. Forty minutes.

It came out smelling of her detergent, which was somehow worse.

By one in the morning she was wearing it. So she opens the app.

She writes: it doesn't smell like him anymore.

It says: it stopped smelling like him, and you noticed.

Then one question. What were you keeping it for?

Fold it and shut the wardrobe, or sleep in it, just tonight.

What would you do?

Twenty-seven days.
ep04:
Twenty-seven days until her ex's wedding, and Zara's best friend has come round to count.

The hoodie stayed folded. That part is going well.

Muting him hid his posts. It did not hide his profile.

Remy asked how many times she had looked.

Remy opened the search history, and started a tally on the takeaway lid.

Five. Ten. Twenty. Forty-one. In four days.

Nobody spoke.

Then Zara laughed, properly, for the first time since she said yes.

Remy left the lid on the table. That night she opens the app.

She writes: forty-one times and nothing changed.

It says: forty-one looks, and he was the same every time.

Then one question. What did you want to be different?

Block him until the wedding, or allow one look a day, at nine, like an adult.

What would you do?

Twenty-six days.
ep05:
It is Friday, and Zara has an alarm set for nine o'clock. It says: one look.

That is the deal. One look a day at the ex whose wedding she said yes to. Twenty-six days.

She is out with work. The plan is one drink.

The first drink agreed with her. So did the second.

At nine the alarm went off in her bag. She looked. Once.

He was at a suit fitting. Navy.

The third drink had opinions about navy.

By eleven, one look had become a habit with a wine list.

In the bathroom she opens the app.

She writes: I only feel fine after two drinks.

No advice. It just asks: what happens to the feeling at drink three?

Go home now, with her coat and her dignity, or stay for one more.

What would you do?

Twenty-five days.
ep06:
At some point last night, Zara liked a photo of her ex from twenty twenty-three.

She found out at eight this morning. His wedding is in twenty-five days, and she said yes to it.

She stayed for one more. One more had friends.

The photo is him on a beach. She took it.

Her like has been sitting under it for seven hours.

Her best friend has seen it. Her best friend sent a screenshot, and no words.

Her passport expired in March. She has a client at ten.

At her desk she opens the app, under the table.

She writes: now he knows I was looking.

It says: he knows you looked, and you're still here.

Then one question. What is the worst thing he could think?

Unlike it and say nothing, or leave it there and own it.

What would you do?

Twenty-four days.
ep07:
Zara is on a dating app at her desk, swiping the way she answers email.

Twenty-four days until her ex's wedding. She said yes. She would now like a plus one.

The like is still there. She left it. He has not mentioned it, which is somehow louder.

So. A profile. Three photos, one with a dog that is not hers.

She swiped through lunch. No. No. No. Owns a kayak. No.

By four she had nine matches and a system. Her director walked past twice.

By midnight one of them had asked her to dinner. A nice man. Spells well.

She opens the other app.

She writes: I want someone on my arm so he sees it.

It says: you want him to see it.

Then one question. Who is the date for?

Zara did not type anything for a while.

Say yes to dinner, or delete the app and go alone.

What would you do?

Twenty-three days.
ep08:
Zara is on a date, in the bar from Friday, talking about her ex.

His wedding is in twenty-three days. She said yes. Tonight was meant to be the fix.

The man is nice. He asked one question. What do you do?

Weddings, she said. And then.

The funny story lasted forty minutes.

The car park. The hoodie. The cake. Lemon.

He nodded in the right places. He ordered olives.

At minute forty-one he asked if she was all right.

On the way home she opens the app.

She writes: I talked about him for forty minutes.

It says: forty minutes, to a stranger, and it still wasn't finished.

Then one question. What did you want the stranger to say?

Text the nice man an apology, or text her ex.

What would you do?

Twenty-two days.
